capabilities.title: Select the verl RL algorithm and infrastructure backend
capabilities.summary: Decide whether verl fits, then pick the advantage estimator, training backend, and rollout engine for the task and scale.

when: Deciding whether to use verl for LLM RL post-training (RLHF, GRPO, PPO, and related algorithms)
Choosing an RL algorithm via algorithm.adv_estimator
Choosing a training backend (FSDP/FSDP2/Megatron) or a rollout engine (vLLM/SGLang/HF)
avoid_when: The task only needs simple SFT or DPO (use TRL or Axolotl)
You need Megatron-native training (use slime or miles)
You want PyTorch-native abstractions with Monarch (use torchforge)

steps: Prefer verl for production-scale RL (tested up to 671B params), backend flexibility, multi-algorithm support, multi-turn tool rollout, or vision-language RL.

Pick algorithm.adv_estimator: grpo (critic-free, math/reasoning), gae (dense rewards, value estimation), reinforce_plus_plus (variance reduction), rloo (leave-one-out baseline), remax (max-reward baseline), or opo (optimal policy optimization).
Pick the training backend via actor_rollout_ref.model.backend: fsdp or fsdp2 for standard scale, megatron for models >70B or expert parallelism.
Pick the rollout engine via actor_rollout_ref.rollout.name: vllm, sglang (required for multi-turn tool calling), or hf.
Note GRPO requires actor_rollout_ref.rollout.n > 1 and actor.use_kl_loss=true; PPO/GAE additionally needs a separate critic model.

capabilities.title: Train a math-reasoning model with GRPO on a GPU cluster
capabilities.summary: Coordinate dataset prep, reward function, config, launch, and monitoring to GRPO-train a reasoning model on tasks like GSM8K or MATH.

when: Training a reasoning model on math tasks (e.g. GSM8K, MATH) with critic-free GRPO
A rule-based/verifiable reward (e.g. exact-match answers) is available
A GPU cluster with 8+ GPUs is available
avoid_when: The task benefits from value-based (GAE) advantage estimation with a critic — use the PPO/GAE workflow instead
Only simple SFT or DPO is needed

expected_outcomes: Reward increases over training steps as the policy improves on the math task

steps: Build train.parquet (and val.parquet) with a `prompt` column (chat messages) and a `reward_model` column carrying `ground_truth`.
Implement the reward function (see custom-reward-function) and point custom_reward_function.path/name at it.

Write the GRPO config: algorithm.adv_estimator=grpo, gamma=1.0, lam=1.0; actor_rollout_ref.rollout.name=vllm, n=8 (must be >1), temperature=0.7, top_p=0.95; actor.use_kl_loss=true, kl_loss_coef=0.001; set data batch/length fields and trainer.n_gpus_per_node=8, total_epochs.
Launch: python3 -m verl.trainer.main_ppo --config-path config --config-name grpo_math (or pass equivalent overrides on the CLI).
Monitor WandB/TensorBoard loss curves, confirm reward is increasing over steps, and evaluate on a held-out test set.

validation: rollout.n > 1 and actor.use_kl_loss=true are set (GRPO requirements)
Reward increases over steps in WandB/TensorBoard
Loss curves are visible and stable
Held-out test-set evaluation is run after training
recovery: CUDA OOM during rollout -> reduce rollout.log_prob_micro_batch_size, enable gradient checkpointing, switch actor.strategy=fsdp2 with offload_policy=true, lower rollout.gpu_memory_utilization
Loss spikes / reward collapse -> lower actor.lr (e.g. 5e-7), raise kl_loss_coef (e.g. 0.01), set max_grad_norm=1.0, reduce clip_ratio to 0.1
Empty batches -> verify the parquet has prompt and reward_model columns and use an absolute train_files path
vLLM generation failures -> pin vllm within the supported range and avoid 0.7.x

capabilities.title: Implement a custom rule-based reward function for verl
capabilities.summary: Write and register a compute_score function that scores a batch of responses against ground truths.

when: The reward is programmatically checkable (e.g. exact-match math answers extracted from generations)
A custom function-based reward is needed instead of a model-based reward
avoid_when: Using a model-based reward via reward_model.path

steps: Create reward.py defining compute_score(responses: list[str], ground_truths: list[str], **kwargs) -> list[float].
For each (response, ground_truth): extract the answer (e.g. regex on \boxed{...}), compare to the ground truth, and append 1.0 for a match else 0.0.
Return a list of float rewards, one per response, in batch order.
Register in config: custom_reward_function.path=/path/to/reward.py and custom_reward_function.name=compute_score (name defaults to compute_score).

validation: The function returns exactly one float per response (len(rewards) == len(responses))
The function name matches custom_reward_function.name (default compute_score)
recovery: Reward not applied / rewards all zero -> confirm custom_reward_function.path is set and the function name matches the configured name
Answer never matches -> verify the extraction regex and ground-truth normalization/whitespace

capabilities.title: Diagnose and fix common verl training failures
capabilities.summary: Apply targeted config changes for OOM, instability, policy collapse, and slow weight sync in a verl PPO/GRPO run.

when: A verl run hits CUDA OOM during rollout or the backward pass
Loss spikes, reward collapses, or training diverges
Entropy drops to zero and outputs become deterministic
There are long pauses between rollout and training phases
avoid_when: The run is healthy (reward increasing, loss stable, no OOM)

expected_outcomes: Run proceeds without CUDA OOM and reward stabilizes after applying the fixes

steps: OOM during rollout: reduce rollout.log_prob_micro_batch_size (e.g. 8->4), enable gradient checkpointing, switch actor.strategy=fsdp2 with fsdp_config.offload_policy=true, and lower rollout.gpu_memory_utilization (0.9->0.7).
OOM during training (backward): reduce actor.ppo_mini_batch_size (64->32), add gradient_accumulation_steps, and enable fsdp mixed_precision=bf16.
Instability / loss spikes: reduce actor.lr (1e-6->5e-7), raise kl_loss_coef (0.001->0.01), set max_grad_norm=1.0, and reduce clip_ratio (0.2->0.1).
Policy collapse (entropy->0): raise rollout.temperature (0.7->0.9), add algorithm.entropy_coef=0.01, and reduce kl_loss_coef.
Slow weight sync: set actor.strategy=fsdp2 for faster resharding and enable trainer.async_weight_update=true.
Re-launch and re-check the same symptom.

validation: No CUDA OOM through rollout and backward
Loss stabilizes and reward recovers or increases
Entropy stays above zero (outputs remain non-deterministic)
No long stalls between rollout and training phases
recovery: Fixes insufficient -> combine batch-size reductions with fsdp2 CPU offload and escalate gradient_accumulation_steps
Weight-sync timeout (Ray actor) -> increase the Ray timeout or set trainer.colocate_actor_ref=true

capabilities.title: Train 70B+ models with the Megatron backend on a multi-node cluster
capabilities.summary: Configure Megatron tensor/pipeline parallelism, convert checkpoints via mbridge, and launch multi-node Ray training for very large models.

when: Requiring expert parallelism or tensor + pipeline model parallelism
avoid_when: The model fits FSDP/FSDP2 on a single node (Megatron adds checkpoint conversion and multi-node overhead)
Running on AMD GPUs (Megatron-LM has a current limitation there)

expected_outcomes: Enables training very large (70B+) models via tensor/pipeline/expert parallelism that would not fit FSDP

steps: Install the Megatron-LM bridge: pip install mbridge.
Convert the HuggingFace model to Megatron format (tools/convert_hf_to_megatron.py) and/or set actor.megatron.use_mbridge=true.
Configure: actor_rollout_ref.model.backend=megatron; actor.strategy=megatron with tensor_model_parallel_size=8, pipeline_model_parallel_size=2; rollout.name=vllm with tensor_parallel_size=8.
Start Ray: on the head node `ray start --head --port=6379`, on workers `ray start --address='head_ip:6379'`.
Launch: python3 -m verl.trainer.main_ppo trainer.nnodes=4 trainer.n_gpus_per_node=8.

validation: The Megatron checkpoint loads without error (use_mbridge enabled if needed)
`ray status` shows all head and worker nodes connected
Training starts and loss/reward are logged
recovery: Megatron checkpoint load fails -> enable megatron.use_mbridge=true and convert HF->Megatron format
NCCL timeout on multi-node -> set NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME, NCCL_IB_DISABLE=0, and raise NCCL_TIMEOUT
Ray cluster connection failures -> check `ray status`, restart the Ray head, verify network connectivity
DeepSpeed 'GPU index out of range' -> export RAY_EXPERIMENTAL_NOSET_CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1

capabilities.title: Pin a compatible vLLM (and CUDA) version for the verl rollout
capabilities.summary: verl's vLLM rollout requires vllm within a supported range; wrong versions cause import errors and generation failures.

when: Installing verl with the vLLM rollout backend
Debugging vLLM import errors, generation hangs, or incorrect rollout outputs
avoid_when: Using the SGLang or HuggingFace rollout backend instead of vLLM

steps: Pin vLLM to the supported range: >=0.8.2 and <=0.12.0 (the SKILL.md quick fix cites >=0.8.5).
Avoid vLLM 0.7.x (known bugs).
For vLLM 0.8.x generation issues, set actor_rollout_ref.rollout.enforce_eager=true to disable CUDA graphs.
vLLM 0.11+ requires CUDA 12.1+ — verify with nvidia-smi.
